f4b_tm_B.hint: T_m = (h_L − h_S)/(s_L − s_S) with B's numbers from the table.

f4b_g_liquid_040.hint: The same formula with the LIQUID g° values, or g_phase("LIQUID", 0.4, 1400.0).

f4b_split_lower_by.hint: Lower of the two homogeneous energies minus the best split's G; both are printed by the brute-force cell.

f4b_f_liquid_1400.hint: Lever rule: f_L = (z − x_S)/(x_L − x_S), printed as f_L in the fsolve cell.

f4b_phase_1600.hint: Type one of "SOLID", "LIQUID" or "both". If the lever rule gives f_L above 1, no split can hold the sample: all of it is one phase. Which one?

f4b_x_liquidus_1600.hint: Row of lens with T = 1600 (third column), or closed_form(1600.0)[1].

f4b_solid_richer.hint: Type "richer" or "poorer". Compare x_S and x_L at the same temperature: a larger x means more B.

f4b_phase_1200.hint: Type one of "SOLID", "LIQUID" or "both". Look at the Phase values pycalphad prints (empty strings are unused vertices).
